findings.issue_text: SQLite ID list construction in pkg/services/annotations/annotationsimpl/xorm_store.go:609 repeatedly formats the accumulated string, causing quadratic runtime and allocation volume for large cleanup batches.

Successful cleanup operations in pkg/services/annotations/annotationsimpl/xorm_store.go:535 and the count and orphan-tag paths are logged at error level, producing false errors even when nothing needs deletion.
Cleanup logs include every selected ID, producing oversized log records for large batches.

goldens.comment: The code uses Error log level for what appears to be debugging information. This will pollute error logs in production. Consider using Debug or Info level instead.

The cleanup job ticker was changed from 10 minutes to 1 minute, which can lead to increased database load and contention due to more frequent execution of cleanup tasks. This change should be reviewed to ensure it aligns with performance expectations.

adjudication_records.issue_text: SQLite ID list construction in pkg/services/annotations/annotationsimpl/xorm_store.go:609 repeatedly formats the accumulated string, causing quadratic runtime and allocation volume for large cleanup batches.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the code in xorm_store.go around line 609, the SQLite ID list construction uses repeated string formatting: `values = fmt.Sprintf("%s, %d", values, v)` in a loop. This is indeed a classic O(n²) string concatenation pattern - each iteration creates a new string by copying the entire previous string plus the new value. For large batches (the test case uses 32767 as batch size), this would cause significant performance degradation and memory allocation overhead. This is a real performance bug in the implementation.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Cleanup logs include every selected ID, producing oversized log records for large batches.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows multiple r.log.Error() calls that include 'ids' in the log output, such as: r.log.Error("Annotations to clean by time", "count", len(ids), "ids", ids, "cond", cond, "err", err). The test case shows annotationCleanupJobBatchSize can be 32767, meaning up to 32767 IDs could be logged in a single log record. This is a real problem - logging potentially tens of thousands of IDs in production log records would create oversized logs and is clearly unintentional debug logging (using Error level for what appears to be debug information).
